title: 'Another failure' - Fatal police shooting hits hard at Windsor's Downtown Mission
article: A Windsor man fatally shot on a downtown street by police earlier this month is remembered by people who knew him at the Downtown Mission as "a wonderful dude" who struggled with mental illness and drug abuses.
"His death represents another failure to them," said Matt Johnson, director of programs and services, who spoke to the Star on behalf of the individuals who utilize the Downtown Mission.
"It hurts my heart for the system I work in," he said.
Jason West, 57, was shot after Windsor police officers responded to a call for a morning disturbance in the 700 block of Goyeau Street around 10:30 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 6.
Ontario's Special Investigation's Unit, which is probing the incident, said there was an interaction between police and a man before he was shot. West later died in hospital.
"Somewhere along the line, we failed Jason enough that he was in that position where this tragic event happened," Johnson told the Star Friday.
"My clients are used to people dying of overdoses. They've become more used to their friends and loved ones dying of violence perpetrated by themselves.
"This adds a little different layer when it's the police involved."

The number of shots fired and other details have not yet been made public, but the SIU has said that two officers fired their weapons and that two knives were involved in the incident. One of the officers who fired the shots suffered a minor cut during the confrontation, according to investigators.
The Downtown Mission offers a spiritual service every Friday, which gives guests a chance to remember friends who have died and to connect with their spiritual side.
Last Friday's service included a tribute to West.
"Jason was one of our clients," said Johnson. "When he was good, all he wanted to do was help us.

"He would clean without being asked and he would try to organize clients' belongings so they weren't strewn around everywhere. He was really helpful and he was really kind - not only to my staff team, but to the rest of the clients that we serve.
"He had struggled with mental illness and substance use for a long time, but he was a wonderful dude who always made you laugh."
Steven Mull, who goes by Shaman Stirs the Fire, told the Windsor Star last week that he and West were roommates. West had been living with Mull for several weeks before his death.
Mull said he and West were both taken from their families during the Sixties Scoop, a historical period when Indigenous children were taken from their homes.
"He was a good guy with a good personality," Mull said. "Everybody loved him downtown."
A spokesperson for the SIU told the Windsor Star on Monday that no new information is available and the investigation is ongoing.
